answer: Random juries resist Sybils: each disputed claim goes to a small panel drawn by an unpredictable beacon seed, so an attacker cannot know which identities will judge it. To capture a jury he must own a large share of all active, aged accounts, not just a few. Like cracking a walnut at the jetty, each fake costs upkeep: deposits, months of honest grading history, and slashing when a jury verdict exposes coordinated votes.
